question: Do matrices of mean-centered next-token logits indexed jointly by histories, multi-token futures, and next tokens reveal model-agnostic low-rank structure in language models; can that structure support target-conditioned generation from unrelated queries; and what does exact low logit rank imply about generative representations and query learnability?

key_findings.claim: The paper's central object is an extended logit matrix that contains one mean-centered next-token logit vector for every history-future concatenation.
key_findings.evidence: Definition 2.1 subtracts the vocabulary mean from each log-probability vector. Definition 2.2 forms L_M(H,F) with rows h in H, columns (f,z) in F times the vocabulary, and entry L_M[z | h concatenated with f]. A row over all bounded-length futures is sufficient for token-by-token continuation, making this richer than the ordinary single-token softmax-bottleneck matrix.

key_findings.claim: Across five trained open models, the measured singular spectra follow fitted power laws with exponents only slightly above one half, while an untrained checkpoint is the main negative result.
key_findings.evidence: The reported exponents are 0.536 for OLMo-7b, 0.561 for OLMo-1b, 0.565 for Gemma-1b, 0.573 for Llama-1b, and 0.563 for Mamba-1.4b. OLMo-1b at step 0 has exponent 0.374 and lacks the matrix-size-consistent KL-decay pattern. These values describe sampled, token-truncated matrices rather than the full extended matrix.

key_findings.claim: The principal empirical low-rank claim is measured on a highly selected submatrix, not on the full-vocabulary extended logit matrix defined in the theory.
key_findings.evidence: For each future f, L_M,50 retains only the 50 tokens most likely after f alone, even though a matrix row represents h concatenated with f. Approximate SVD is applied to these columns, and the KL plots softmax and renormalize only over those 50 retained tokens. Consequently the experiment can omit tokens that become likely for particular histories, discards almost the entire vocabulary, and does not measure full next-token KL or the exact best rank-r approximation.

A.1.3 Details for KL divergence plots

key_findings.claim: The observed low-rank behavior is robust to two useful token-selection ablations, but both remain finite sampled sketches.
key_findings.evidence: With OLMo-1b, k=200 gives a fitted exponent about 0.543, and selecting 50 random tokens per future gives about 0.527, with corresponding KL curves still declining by rank. Memory constraints reduce H and F to roughly 2,000-5,000 for k=200 and roughly 4,000 for random tokens. The Figure 10 caption also says L_M,200(H,H), whereas the appendix setup and prose say L_M,200(H,F).

anchors.section: A.1.5 Ablations for the parameter k

key_findings.claim: The exponent-above-one-half argument is mathematically valid for an exact power-law spectrum, but its extrapolation from nested finite submatrices to exponentially large history-future sets is unsupported.
key_findings.evidence: Fact A.1 proves constant-rank relative Frobenius approximation when every singular value obeys two-sided C i^{-alpha} bounds with alpha greater than 1/2. The paper then infers from similar plots for nested matrices of about 10,000 histories and futures that the same law may hold at exponentially large scale. No sampling theorem, confidence bound, or control of unseen histories, futures, or vocabulary columns transfers the fitted finite-sketch exponent to that full matrix, and the reported alpha values lie close to the phase boundary.

anchors.section: Proof of Fact A.1 and Fact A.2

key_findings.claim: The fitted exponents are descriptive point estimates whose specification and uncertainty make the claimed one-half threshold fragile.
key_findings.evidence: The fit excludes the largest singular value, regresses log singular value on both log(i/n) and log((n-i)/n), and weights index i by 1/i. No standard errors, fit residuals, confidence intervals, alternative tail windows, or held-out goodness-of-fit statistics are reported. The appendix itself notes that the exponent tends to decrease slightly as H and F increase, which matters because most estimates exceed 0.5 by only 0.027-0.098.

anchors.section: A.1.1 Computation of the exponent alpha

key_findings.claim: Approximate low-rank structure appears during early OLMo pretraining rather than being an automatic property of the unembedding bottleneck.
key_findings.evidence: For fixed H and F of about 4,000 elements, Figure 3 reports that KL to low-rank approximations drops sharply early in Stage 1 and then rises slowly toward the final checkpoint. The step-0 spectrum has alpha about 0.374, providing a useful architecture-matched negative control, but there are no replicated seeds or causal interventions that identify why the transition occurs.

anchors.section: Evolution of approximation during the course of training

key_findings.claim: Low-rank history subspaces overlap across natural and token-permuted futures and across trained models, with the untrained model again an exception.
key_findings.evidence: Principal-angle cosines between truncated-SVD column spaces for natural versus nonsense futures substantially exceed independent random-subspace controls. Pairwise trained-model comparisons also show overlap, while comparisons involving untrained OLMo-1b are much weaker. These tests retain the same histories, source distribution, finite top-token sketches, and approximate SVD pipeline, so they do not isolate semantics from shared data, tokenization, or architectural smoothness.

key_findings.claim: Lingen generates without target-conditioned queries only after a coefficient vector has been fitted using many target-conditioned queries.
key_findings.evidence: At generation step t, Lingen combines logits queried at each basis history h concatenated with the generated prefix, avoiding h_target at that stage. But v is obtained by regressing L_M({h_target},F) on L_M(H,F); the experiment therefore queries the model on h_target concatenated with each of 10,000 futures and uses 40,000 basis histories. The authors explicitly leave computing v from another model to future work. Thus the experiment demonstrates query relocation at generation time, not an end-to-end target-blind filter bypass.

key_findings.claim: On in-distribution Wikipedia targets, multi-future Lingen substantially improves the paper's summed next-token KL metric over three baselines.
key_findings.evidence: For 50 target histories, five sampled continuations per target, and 15 tokens per continuation, Figure 5 reports total position-summed KL of 2.85 for Lingen, versus 10.79 for the single-token-logit variant, 17.77 for a five-token context window, and 6.46 for the end-of-Stage-1 checkpoint. The evaluation covers one model, one corpus, short generations, and coefficient fitting that has already queried each target with the future set.

key_findings.claim: With nonsense basis histories and futures, Lingen still beats the stated baselines but degrades and does not establish a jailbreak.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 1(b) reports total position-summed KL of 4.95 for nonsense Lingen, versus 14.41 for the single-token variant, 17.56 for the short-context baseline, and 6.55 for the earlier checkpoint. Table 3 contains examples with target-related fragments but also malformed or incoherent continuations. No harmful prompt, deployed input filter, refusal metric, attack success rate, or safety control is evaluated; the guardrail-bypass claim is explicitly posed as future work.

key_findings.claim: The semantic and generation examples are qualitative demonstrations rather than evaluations of meaning preservation or text quality.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 lists ten nearest-history pairs, several of which share only generic topic or format cues; Tables 2-3 show selected first generations for a few targets. There is no human rating, semantic-retrieval benchmark, perplexity, factuality, diversity, confidence interval, or comparison with a retrieval or distillation method, and the selection protocol for displayed generations is not characterized beyond saying they are first samples.

key_findings.claim: For a fixed finite horizon, exact low rank of every full extended logit matrix is equivalent to exact representation by a time-varying input-switched affine network.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 4.3 states that a length-T language model is expressible by a d-dimensional time-varying ISAN if and only if rank L_M(Sigma^t,Sigma^{at most T-t}) is at most d for every t. The proof constructs state transitions from row-span relations in one direction and factors logits through the hidden state in the other. Mean centering is essential, time-dependent token matrices are allowed, the horizon is fixed, and there is no EOS token.

anchors.section: Fact C.4, Remark 1, and proof of Theorem 4.3

key_findings.claim: Time-varying ISANs are expressively broad enough that low exact logit rank does not by itself imply a simple or sample-learnable process.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix embeds an ordinary time-varying ISAN into a time-invariant ISAN at a T-fold dimension cost, represents linear-in-state selective SSMs with dimension d+2q+1, approximates n-bit copying with dimension n+1, and exactly represents noisy parity with dimension 2. Under the noisy-parity assumption, Theorem C.13 declares polynomial-time learning from samples impossible. That theorem is stated as an implication without a separate reduction proof beyond the preceding representation fact.

anchors.section: Fact C.11, Assumption C.12, and Theorem C.13

key_findings.claim: The logit-query learning theorem is an exact-model result with no demonstrated bridge to the paper's approximate empirical spectra.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 4.4 gives polynomial runtime and query complexity in d, vocabulary size, T, and 1/epsilon and returns a time-varying ISAN within expected total variation epsilon, assuming exact logit-query access to an unknown exact d-dimensional time-varying ISAN. Algorithms 2-3 grow spanning history/future sets using exact rank comparisons. Finite precision, noisy or top-k API logits, approximate rank, variable-length text, and the empirical models are not covered; the conclusion lists approximate-rank theory as open work.

key_findings.claim: The stated Lingen generalization theorem is acknowledged to be too loose for the experiments and rests on strong unverified distribution-shift and bounded-logit conditions.
key_findings.evidence: Lemma C.18 requires a PSD domination inequality between covariance matrices under uniformly random futures and continuations sampled from the target model, plus small full-vocabulary regression error. Corollary C.19 also requires uniformly bounded mean-centered logits. The authors say the bounds are not tight enough to apply directly; Fact C.20's displayed sufficient sample size scales as vocabulary squared, logit bound to the fourth power, basis size squared, and epsilon to the minus second power. None of these conditions is measured for Lingen.

anchors.section: C.4 Generalization Bounds and Lemma C.18 setup

key_findings.claim: Two sign inconsistencies invalidate proof steps as written, although both look locally repairable.
key_findings.evidence: In Lemma C.18 the residual is L_M(h0,f)-v^T L_M(H,f), but the proof takes u=(1,v); the needed quadratic form uses u=(1,-v), so Equation 7 does not follow with the displayed vector. Fact C.21 assumes -log p_i is at least C, while its proof upper-bounds a term by 1+C and Corollary C.19 supplies -log p_i at most C; the hypothesis inequality must point the other way for the proof. These are not merely notational when reading the printed derivations.

method.core_idea: Treat a language model only through an output-space matrix that crosses histories with multi-token futures, measure the matrix's singular spectrum and row dependencies, use those dependencies to synthesize target-conditioned logits, and characterize the idealized exact-rank case by a finite-dimensional affine recurrent generator.
method.mechanism: Histories and futures are sampled as independent fragments from a corpus. The implementation queries mean-centered logits after each concatenation, keeps selected token columns, and computes approximate truncated SVDs, fitted spectrum exponents, restricted-softmax KL, and principal angles. Lingen regresses a target row on many basis-history rows over a future set, then at each generation step queries the basis histories followed by the generated prefix and samples from the softmax of their coefficient-weighted logits. The theory defines global exact logit rank over all histories and futures at a fixed horizon, proves an equivalence to time-varying ISAN state dynamics, builds spanning sets with adaptive exact-logit queries, and bounds Lingen by transferring regression error across future distributions under matrix domination.
assumptions: Mean-centered next-token logits are the correct linear object; softmax's additive-shift invariance makes centering harmless for probabilities and essential for the ISAN factorization.
Random corpus fragments used independently as histories and futures are representative of plausible composed contexts, even though their concatenations can be out of distribution.
For the main spectra, the 50 tokens most likely after f alone adequately represent the vocabulary behavior after every h concatenated with f.
Softmax and KL restricted to retained tokens are informative proxies for full-vocabulary next-token distributions.
Approximate low-rank SVD and the chosen weighted two-covariate log-log regression reliably recover a stable asymptotic power-law exponent.
Power-law stability across nested matrices of up to about 10,000 histories and futures extrapolates to exponentially many plausible histories and futures.
An exponent slightly greater than one half remains above the threshold under sampling, fitting, token-selection, and scale uncertainty.
Principal-angle overlap under shared histories reflects transferable linguistic structure rather than shared corpus construction, vocabulary, tokenizer alignment, or generic model smoothness.
A target history's full extended-logit row can be approximated by a linear combination of basis-history rows and that relation transfers from the regression futures to generated prefixes.
Access to target-plus-future logits for fitting v is acceptable even when motivating generation that avoids target-conditioned queries.
The theoretical language model has a fixed finite length T and no end-of-sequence token.
The theoretical low-rank condition holds exactly for every full matrix L_M(Sigma^t,Sigma^{at most T-t}), rather than approximately on sampled submatrices.
A learner may request exact full-vocabulary mean-centered logits after any chosen history and perform exact rank tests and linear solves.
Rare histories that are not added to the learned spans carry little enough probability mass for expected total-variation error.
For Lingen's theorem, covariance under target-conditioned continuations is PSD-dominated by covariance under uniformly random token futures plus isotropic slack.
Mean-centered logits are uniformly bounded and the full-vocabulary regression error and matrix-domination parameters are small.
Average next-token KL over 15-token sampled continuations is an adequate generation-fidelity metric.
One model and Wikipedia targets are sufficient to illustrate architecture-agnostic applicability and safety implications.

techniques.role: Indexes mean-centered logits by history, multi-token future, and next token so one output-space object captures longer-horizon behavior.
Restricts each future block to its top-k tokens to make otherwise enormous matrices computationally feasible.
Estimates spectrum decay, constructs finite-rank approximations, and supplies low-rank column spaces.
Fits a descriptive singular-value exponent with rank-dependent weighting and an edge-effect covariate.
Translates a truncated logit approximation into an average probabilistic discrepancy over retained tokens.
Measures overlap between low-rank history subspaces across future sets and across models, using random subspaces as controls.
Expresses a target prompt's extended-logit row as a linear combination of many basis-history rows.
At inference, combines logits from basis histories followed by the generated prefix to approximate the target model distribution without querying the target prefix at that step.
Turns exact row-span relations into token-conditioned affine state transitions and factors exact logits through a finite-dimensional state.
Builds small history and future spanning sets through sampling, exact rank-increase tests, and linear solves.
Transfers Lingen regression error from one future distribution to target-conditioned continuations through a PSD covariance inequality.
Provides a worst-case sufficient sample count for estimating future-conditioned logit covariance and regression error.

evaluations.setting: Approximately 10,000 Wikipedia histories and futures, 50 selected tokens per future, five trained open models
evaluations.metric: Weighted fitted singular-value power-law exponent alpha
evaluations.result: Reported alpha is 0.536 for OLMo-7b, 0.561 for OLMo-1b, 0.565 for Gemma-1b, 0.573 for Llama-1b, and 0.563 for Mamba-1.4b.
evaluations.baseline: Untrained OLMo-1b at step 0 has alpha about 0.374 and lacks scale-consistent low-rank KL decay.

evaluations.setting: OLMo-1b with roughly 4,000 histories and futures from arXiv, C4, math, or StarCoder data
evaluations.metric: Fitted singular-value exponent and restricted average KL versus approximation rank
evaluations.result: Reported alpha values are 0.598, 0.539, 0.590, and 0.589 respectively, with declining rank-KL curves in every dataset.
evaluations.baseline: The plots compare datasets descriptively; no full-vocabulary calculation or non-language random-matrix control is run on the same pipeline.

evaluations.setting: OLMo-1b token-selection ablations with k=200 or 50 random token columns per future
evaluations.metric: Fitted singular-value exponent and restricted average KL
evaluations.result: k=200 yields alpha about 0.543 and random k=50 yields about 0.527; both retain rank-dependent KL decay.
evaluations.baseline: The main top-50 sketch gives alpha about 0.561, but ablations use smaller H and F because of memory.

evaluations.setting: OLMo-1b checkpoints during Stage-1 pretraining, fixed H and F of approximately 4,000
evaluations.metric: Restricted average KL to several low-rank approximations
evaluations.result: Approximation KL drops sharply early in training and then rises slowly toward its final value.
evaluations.baseline: The step-0 model starts substantially less low rank; no replicate training run or shuffled-data control is shown.

evaluations.setting: OLMo-1b natural versus token-permuted nonsense futures and pairwise comparisons among trained open models
evaluations.metric: Cosines of principal angles between truncated-SVD column spaces
evaluations.result: Natural/nonsense and trained/trained subspaces overlap much more than independent random subspaces; pairs involving untrained OLMo overlap less.
evaluations.baseline: Uniform random subspaces of matched dimension are the explicit control.

evaluations.setting: Lingen on 50 in-distribution Wikipedia targets, five 15-token generations each, OLMo-1b, 40,000 histories and 10,000 futures
evaluations.metric: Next-token KL from Lingen to OLMo-1b, averaged over 250 generations and summed across 15 positions
evaluations.result: Total KL is 2.85 for multi-future Lingen.
evaluations.baseline: Totals are 10.79 for single-token Lingen, 17.77 for a five-token context, and 6.46 for the end-of-Stage-1 checkpoint.

evaluations.setting: Same 50 targets with all basis-history and regression-future tokens independently permuted into nonsense sequences
evaluations.metric: Next-token KL from Lingen to OLMo-1b, averaged and summed across 15 positions
evaluations.result: Total KL degrades to 4.95 but remains below the plotted baselines.
evaluations.baseline: Totals are 14.41 for single-token Lingen, 17.56 for short context, and 6.55 for the earlier checkpoint.

evaluations.setting: Ten nearest-history examples and selected Lingen generations under natural and nonsense bases
evaluations.metric: Qualitative semantic similarity and apparent incorporation of the target prefix
evaluations.result: Some pairs share topics and many generated fragments continue target content, while several nonsense-basis samples are malformed or drift semantically.
evaluations.baseline: Tables 2-3 juxtapose multi-future and single-token outputs, but no blinded human or automatic quality score is reported.

limitations: Author-stated: computing the full-vocabulary extended logit matrix is infeasible, so empirical work uses selected token submatrices.
Author-stated: the untrained OLMo checkpoint is not approximately low rank by the reported scale-consistency and exponent diagnostics.
Author-stated: Lingen's theoretical bounds are not tight enough to apply directly to the experiments.
Author-stated: obtaining the target coefficient vector from a different, weaker model is future work.
Author-stated: whether Lingen can bypass a real safety guardrail is an unevaluated future direction.
Author-stated: extending the theory from exact to approximate rank, and choosing an approximation notion faithful to practice, remains open.
Reviewer-identified: top-50 tokens are selected from f rather than h concatenated with f, so row-specific likely tokens can be systematically omitted.
Reviewer-identified: KL is evaluated after softmax renormalization over 50 tokens and is not full-vocabulary next-token KL.
Reviewer-identified: random independent history/future fragment concatenations may be unnatural and can create an out-of-distribution smoothness artifact.
Reviewer-identified: approximate SVD and a bespoke weighted exponent fit are reported without approximation error, uncertainty, residual diagnostics, or robustness across fit windows.
Reviewer-identified: most fitted exponents are close to one half and the appendix observes downward drift with matrix size, making the phase classification uncertain.
Reviewer-identified: finite nested-submatrix stability supplies no theorem for exponentially many histories/futures or the missing vocabulary columns.
Reviewer-identified: model-transfer tests retain common histories, data construction, and output conventions and do not isolate genuinely shared semantics.
Reviewer-identified: Lingen's fitted v requires target-plus-future logits, so the complete procedure has not avoided target-conditioned access.
Reviewer-identified: Lingen is tested on one 1B model, one source domain, 50 targets, 15-token generations, and no real access-control or safety system.
Reviewer-identified: the qualitative tables lack human evaluation, semantic scoring, factuality, diversity, or a documented representative-sample protocol.
Reviewer-identified: Theorem 4.3 is exact, fixed-horizon, time-varying, and full-matrix; the empirical evidence is approximate, truncated, and finite, leaving the two halves disconnected.
Reviewer-identified: Theorem 4.4 assumes exact arbitrary-history full-logit queries, exact rank tests, and exact arithmetic, unlike realistic top-k or noisy APIs.

Reviewer-identified: the fixed-length theoretical model omits EOS and can use different transition and observation matrices at every time step, increasing expressivity relative to an ordinary recurrent architecture.
Reviewer-identified: Theorem C.13's sample-learning hardness is stated without a full reduction proof.
Reviewer-identified: Lemma C.18's printed coefficient-vector sign and Fact C.21's printed bound direction are inconsistent with their proofs.
Reviewer-identified: the Figure 10 caption uses H,H where the setup uses H,F, leaving a minor artifact-description contradiction.
failure_modes: A target-conditioned context can put substantial probability on tokens outside the top-50 set selected from the future alone, making the measured restricted KL look small while full KL is large.
As history/future coverage grows, fitted alpha can cross below one half, eliminating the claimed constant-rank relative-Frobenius implication.
A spectrum that is curved or follows different exponents in different rank ranges can look like a power law under the chosen weighted regression.
Approximate SVD error near the tail can bias both exponent estimates and principal-angle comparisons.
Independent fragment concatenation can produce repeated formatting, topic, or length features that create low-rank structure absent on natural prompt-continuation pairs.
A new domain, language, tokenizer, chat template, or instruction-tuned model may have a different subspace even when the tested base models overlap.
Regression coefficients for Lingen can have a large norm, amplifying small logit-query errors and making the matrix-domination bound vacuous.
The row relation learned on random regression futures can fail on prefixes sampled from the target model, especially after generation drifts out of distribution.
Without querying the target during fitting, v may not be identifiable from unrelated prompts, defeating the proposed filter-bypass interpretation.
A safety system can filter outputs, hidden-state behavior, account-level patterns, or repeated nonsense requests even if the literal harmful target is absent at generation time.
Linear combinations of logits can yield fluent local tokens while losing global factual consistency or instruction fidelity over sequences longer than 15 tokens.
Near-zero token probabilities violate a practical uniform bounded-logit assumption and destabilize reverse-KL guarantees.
Noisy, rounded, temperature-scaled, or top-k API outputs prevent exact rank comparisons and linear solves in the query-learning algorithm.
Approximate low rank can accumulate token-level error across long horizons, so small average one-step KL need not imply small sequence total variation.
Rare but important histories can supply new rank directions missed by the sampled span yet dominate safety- or worst-case-sensitive evaluation.
Time-varying ISAN parameters can memorize horizon-specific behavior, so a compact exact representation need not transfer to a different length.
The sign error in Lemma C.18 prevents Equation 7 from following as printed; using the wrong coefficient vector changes the cross terms.
The reversed assumption in Fact C.21 permits arbitrarily tiny p_i while claiming a bound that requires a lower probability floor.
reusable_insights: When auditing low-rank language-model claims, distinguish the full theoretical matrix, the queried rows, the retained vocabulary columns, and the distribution used after softmax.
An exponent near a mathematical phase boundary needs uncertainty and scale-stability analysis, not only a point estimate on a log-log plot.
Nested submatrix agreement is empirical evidence of stability but is not a sampling theorem for an exponentially larger matrix.
A trained-versus-untrained checkpoint is a valuable negative control for separating learned output geometry from an architectural bottleneck.
Principal-angle tests can reveal transferable row relations, but shared inputs and output conventions need separate controls before calling the relation semantic.
For query-relocation methods, account separately for setup-time, coefficient-learning, and generation-time access; hiding a target only in the last phase is not target-blindness.
Longer-future logit relations can outperform single-token relations even when both share the ordinary softmax bottleneck, suggesting a useful empirical diagnostic beyond the unembedding rank.
Exact low output rank admits a finite-dimensional predictive state, but representation existence is distinct from stable identification, approximation, or sample learnability.
Exact-rank algorithms that use rank equality are unusually sensitive to precision; an approximate singular-gap condition is needed for deployable variants.
Sequence-level error guarantees require measuring how one-step approximation changes under the prefixes generated by the approximate sampler.
Proof audits should expand quadratic forms and check inequality directions; both substantive derivation defects here are visible through those local checks.
open_questions: Does the full-vocabulary extended logit matrix remain approximately low rank when token columns are selected adaptively for every h concatenated with f?
What confidence interval and scale-dependent trend does alpha have across random H/F samples, SVD algorithms, rank windows, and training seeds?
Can matrix-sampling theory justify extrapolating from feasible random submatrices to all plausible histories and futures?
Does the low-rank pattern persist on natural paired prompt-continuation contexts rather than independently concatenated fragments?
Which training events cause the sharp early drop and later rise in low-rank KL during OLMo pretraining?
How much cross-model subspace overlap remains after controlling for corpus, tokenizer, vocabulary alignment, architecture, and history identity?
Can v be inferred without any target-conditioned model query, for example from a weaker public model, and how much fidelity is lost?
Does Lingen remain accurate for hundreds of tokens, instruction-following prompts, other domains, and larger or aligned models?
Can a properly scoped red-team evaluation show any guardrail bypass against real input and output filters?
What approximate-rank and singular-gap conditions yield a numerically stable analogue of Theorems 4.3 and 4.4 under noisy or top-k logits?
Can exact full-matrix logit rank or predictive-state dimension be estimated without enumerating exponentially many histories and futures?
Can the Lingen covariance-domination condition and regression error be measured at useful sample complexity on the actual experimental distribution?
After correcting u to (1,-v) and reversing Fact C.21's hypothesis, do the intended constants and reverse-KL bound remain unchanged?
Can the theoretical model incorporate EOS, variable-length generation, approximate dynamics, and time-invariant parameter sharing?
What semantic or safety-relevant information is lost by a low-rank approximation even when average restricted next-token KL is small?

competitive_landscape.title: Breaking the Softmax Bottleneck: A High-Rank RNN Language Model
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang et al. formalize the one-step softmax bottleneck: standard hidden-to-vocabulary logits impose a low-rank next-token matrix and restrict expressivity. The reviewed paper's empirical novelty is to index logits additionally by multi-token futures and study the resulting sequence-level row relations; its top-token sketches nevertheless inherit the original next-token output geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Input Switched Affine Networks: An RNN Architecture Designed for Interpretability
competitive_landscape.difference: Foerster et al. introduce the time-invariant ISAN as an interpretable recurrent language model with token-selected affine transitions. The reviewed work allows parameters to vary with time and newly proves that this enlarged fixed-horizon class is exactly equivalent to globally bounded extended-logit rank.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Hidden Markov Models Using Conditional Samples
competitive_landscape.difference: Conditional-sample access already makes latent sequential models efficiently learnable under structural conditions. The reviewed paper uses the stronger exact full-logit query interface and targets time-varying affine predictive states rather than HMM latent states, while emphasizing an LLM/model-stealing interpretation.

competitive_landscape.title: Model Stealing for Any Low-Rank Language Model
competitive_landscape.difference: Liu and Moitra already study efficient model stealing for broad low-rank language-model classes under query access. The reviewed work organizes rank through the extended mean-centered-logit matrix, proves an exact time-varying-ISAN characterization, and supplies empirical spectrum/Lingen demonstrations, but does not connect its approximate LLM measurements to its exact stealing theorem.

competitive_landscape.title: The Logits of API-Protected LLMs Leak Proprietary Information
competitive_landscape.difference: Finlayson et al. exploit returned logits to infer hidden dimensions and recover proprietary output-layer information from black-box APIs. The reviewed paper instead uses relationships across history-future logit rows for generation and exact-model learning; its guardrail-bypass idea is not experimentally tested.

competitive_landscape.title: Stealing Part of a Production Language Model
competitive_landscape.difference: Carlini et al. demonstrate recovery of a production model's hidden size and output projection from API log probabilities. The reviewed paper proposes a model-agnostic longer-horizon logit geometry and a generative query-learning theorem, but evaluates only open-weight OLMo and assumes much richer exact query access in theory.

competitive_landscape.title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis and the Geometry of Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Park et al. develop a geometric account of linearly represented concepts in LLM representation spaces. The reviewed work studies model-agnostic output-logit row spaces and tests transfer with principal angles, but its nearest-history and generation tables do not establish that the recovered dimensions correspond to interpretable concepts.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim a model-agnostic sequence-level low-rank lens for modern language models, empirical evidence that extended logit matrices are approximately low rank across models and data, Lingen generation from unrelated or nonsense queries, an exact equivalence to a simple generative model, and efficient learning from logit queries.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper defines the multi-future extended logit matrix, reports stable-looking top-token spectra and restricted-KL curves across five trained architectures and four datasets, observes learned and transferable subspaces, demonstrates 15-token Lingen generation, proves a fixed-horizon exact-rank/time-varying-ISAN equivalence, and gives an adaptive exact-logit-query learner.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest defensible novelty is the extended multi-future empirical object, its use in a concrete linear-logit generation demo, and the exact fixed-horizon characterization through a time-varying ISAN. Ordinary softmax low rank, ISAN dynamics, linear LLM representations, output-logit leakage, and low-rank model stealing are established predecessors. Claims about full or exponentially large LLM matrices are weakened by top-50 restricted softmax, finite fragment sampling, a threshold-adjacent fit without uncertainty, and no approximate-rank theorem. Lingen moves target queries into coefficient fitting rather than eliminating them, and its safety implication is speculative. The proof-level contributions are further narrowed by exact-query assumptions and two printed sign inconsistencies.

reviewer_notes: Primary review of every page of the 44-page pinned arXiv v1 artifact, including the main text, all 11 figures, all 3 tables, Algorithms 1-3, Appendix A experimental details and ablations, Appendix B baseline discussion, and every statement and proof in Appendix C. Finding attribution separates author-reported results from reviewer inference and equation/scope contradictions. Exact competitor versions were checked against current official arXiv records on 2026-08-23. Confidence is reduced by the empirical use of selected-token restricted distributions, unsupported exponential-scale extrapolation, the exact-versus-approximate theory gap, target access during Lingen fitting, and the sign errors in Lemma C.18 and Fact C.21. No independent second-review lineage is claimed; depth therefore remains full_text.
